issues.legal_issue: A dispute over whether a person occupying agricultural land became a tenant under the persons to whom the land was allotted must be determined by the designated revenue authority when the tenancy legislation assigns that question to it.
material_facts: A lessee was inducted onto the land by a co-sharer while a partition suit was pending.
In execution of the partition decree, the land was allotted to other co-sharers, who sought actual possession.
The occupant claimed that he was a tenant protected by the applicable tenancy legislation, and the co-sharers disputed that he was their tenant.
The tenancy legislation assigned the determination of tenant status to revenue authorities and excluded civil-court jurisdiction over matters assigned to those authorities.
issues.conclusion: The disputed question whether the occupant had become a tenant under the co-sharers fell within the exclusive jurisdiction of the revenue authorities; the civil court could not decide it, even though the co-sharers relied on the effect of the pending partition proceedings on the lease.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 132 and 133 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, read with section 112B, assign tenant-status questions to the statutory authorities and exclude civil-court jurisdiction over those questions. Section 142(1A), together with the protections originating under the Mysore Tenants (Temporary Protection from Eviction) Act, 1961, continued protection against eviction for a qualifying tenant. Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, might support the co-sharers’ position on the merits, but did not permit the civil court to decide the tenancy question assigned to the revenue authorities. The Court followed Bhimji Shankar Kulkarni v. Dundappa Vithappa Adapudi and Dhondi Tukaram Mali v. Hari Dadu Mang; it distinguished Mussamiya Imam Haider Bux Razvi v. Rabari Govindbhai Ratnabhai and Corporation of the City of Bangalore v. B. T. Kampanna.

predicates.partition_execution_proceeding: A party seeks possession through execution of a decree dividing agricultural land.
predicates.tenant_status_disputed: The parties dispute whether an occupant of the land is a tenant, including whether the occupant became a tenant under the persons who received the land.
predicates.tenancy_status_assigned_to_special_tribu: The applicable legal scheme assigns the disputed tenant-status question to a designated tribunal or revenue authority.

issues.definition: When execution of a land-division decree gives rise to a disputed tenant-status question assigned to a special tribunal, that tribunal must decide the question.

issues.legal_issue: Actual possession under an executed partition decree depends on the revenue authority’s final determination of the occupant’s protected tenant status.
material_facts: The co-sharers sought actual delivery of land allotted to them under a partition decree.
The occupant was in cultivating possession and claimed protection as a tenant.
The tenant-status dispute had to be determined by the revenue authorities.
The Court directed that actual possession be delivered if the tenancy claim was finally rejected, and that only symbolic possession be delivered if the claim was finally upheld.
issues.conclusion: The co-sharers could receive actual possession if the revenue authorities finally determined that the occupant was not a tenant; if the authorities determined that he was a tenant, they could receive only symbolic possession.
issues.legal_principle: The applicable tenancy protections prevent actual eviction of a qualifying tenant except in accordance with the governing legislation. Because the tenancy question belongs to the revenue authorities, delivery of possession in execution must reflect their final determination. The Court applied the protections under the Mysore Tenants (Temporary Protection from Eviction) Act, 1961, and sections 22 and 142(1A) of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961.

predicates.partition_decree_execution: A party seeks delivery of land through execution of a decree dividing that land.
predicates.tenant_status_finally_determined_by_spec: The designated authority has finally decided whether the occupant has protected tenant status.
predicates.special_authority_finds_tenant: The designated authority finds that the occupant is a protected tenant.
predicates.special_authority_rejects_tenancy: The designated authority rejects the occupant’s claim to tenant status.

issues.definition: In execution of a land-division decree, the final tenant-status determination controls whether possession is delivered actually or symbolically.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant-status plea does not by itself require referral to a special tribunal, and civil-court jurisdiction must be assessed by determining whether a genuine issue assigned to that tribunal arises.
material_facts: The occupant raised a tenancy-protection plea during execution proceedings and in appeals concerning delivery of possession.
Earlier orders directing delivery of possession had been made, and the co-sharers argued that those orders had become final.
The record also raised whether the questions in the appeals were within the tribunal’s competence and whether the statutory restriction applied to the appellate court.
In a separate opinion, Justice Kailasam stated that the High Court should have examined those questions and that a court must be satisfied that a tenancy issue actually arises before referring it.
issues.conclusion: In the separate opinion, Justice Kailasam concluded that the High Court should have examined whether a genuine tenancy issue arose, whether the earlier possession orders had become final, and whether the tribunal could decide the questions; a defendant’s plea alone did not settle the jurisdictional question.
issues.legal_principle: Justice Kailasam applied the principle that exclusion of civil-court jurisdiction is not lightly inferred and must be expressed or clearly implied by the relevant enactment. He relied on sections 132 and 133 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, and distinguished the provision for staying suits from execution proceedings and civil appeals. He relied on Bhatia Cooperative Housing Society v. D. C. Patel, Raizada Topandas v. M/s. Gorakhram Gokhalchand, Vasudeva Gopalkrishna Tanwaker v. Board of Liquidators, Happy Home Co-operative Housing Society, Mussamiya Imam Haider Bux Razvi v. Rabari Govindbhai Ratnabhai, Bhimji Shankar Kulkarni v. Dundappa Vithappa Adapudi, and Corporation of the City of Bangalore v. B. T. Kampanna. This was the reasoning of the separate opinion; the appeals were dismissed by the Court.

predicates.civil_execution_or_appeal_proceeding: The matter before the civil court is an execution proceeding or an appeal concerning execution rather than an ordinary trial of a suit.
predicates.tenant_status_pleaded: A party asserts that an occupant is a tenant protected by tenancy legislation.
predicates.genuine_tenancy_issue_not_yet_establishe: The court has not determined that the facts raise a genuine tenant-status question assigned to the special tribunal.

issues.definition: In an execution proceeding or appeal, a tenancy allegation alone does not require referral unless the court determines that a genuine tribunal-assigned tenancy issue arises.
